Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
> Xaddam wrote:
> I suppose it is kinda fragile. I don't think it's fragile because card flow, since it is a 65 card deck (and can easily be 60). But 11 caps with limited combat defense and few bounces are risky.
>
I gave it a try yesterday. Well, its main problem is that, in order to function, you need exactly the right order of cards if you want to survive (you really need Flurry to untap - without untapped vamp you can't defend yourself, and in order to be offensive you need to act (bleed), which has to be via Flurry and which has to not be blocked - and you don't have that much stealth).

Also, this is a rather irresponsible bleed deck. I swapped some odd stealth for 3 Spying Missions, but still, your goal is to bleed hard on lots of stealth.

Another also, this crypt is, well, lacking - my last game I had Mistress, 2 Adanas and Keith - once Mistress ended up beaten (yeah, Obediences do diddly squat if you can't untap), Adana's lack of any kind of DOM became a major problem.

I don't know, I gave this deck three tries, had some ousts but it is very unstable and very luck-dependant. Perhaps I should make a version that is less aggressive but has more consistent untap, either some kind of DOM FOR obf g1-2 Ventrues or some version of Tremeres with Rutors.

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
I didn't watch the episode, but is this IC Flurry deck by any chance related to Benoit Moyen's  Order 66

Because if it is, then no, it's not very new and yes, it's very fragile but not because of cardflow or stealth. If you're getting beaten up while tapped out that's not the deck's fault and if you get stuck without Flurry's then that's an issue that's easily fixed with proper discards and use of Dreams. Also, bleeding for 3 is fairly responsible to start with and between deflection cancels (Approximation of Loyalty) and block denial you shouldn't really be ousting your grandprey.

The reason it's fragile is that it's such a small deck (which is needed to get the required cardflow) and that if your predator sports a combination of bounce and intercept, it's non-trivial to secure the gamewin before running out of deck.

If it's not that deck, then ignore me

Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
> Izaak wrote:
> If you're getting beaten up while tapped out that's not the deck's fault
>
Well, it depends who you're preying on, but if your Flurry bleeds get blocked, then you end up tapped, and yes, this deck very much relies on getting those Flurry bleeds through (otherwise you end up with handful of reaction cards you can't use)

> Izaak wrote:
> Also, bleeding for 3 is fairly responsible to start with and between deflection cancels (Approximation of Loyalty) and block denial you shouldn't really be ousting your grandprey.
>
Eh, you bleed, prey blocks, you NEED to stealth (otherwise, you don't untap yadda yadda) and now we have a bleed of 3 on stealth. Not everyone that bounces is cap 6 or less and every bleed this deck makes is a hefty one.

Far from it that this isn't a good deck - if I thought otherwise I wouldn't have constructed it - but it turns out I like my decks a bit more stable.

EDIT: sorry for double post, my mistake.

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
Well fair enough, but I didn't really encounter those issues when I played a slightly tweaked version of it. Granted, that was a few years ago so the meta might be different, but I think that it should still be exceptionally strong in an environment where people play more competitive decks.

> Eh, you bleed, prey blocks, you NEED to stealth (otherwise, you don't untap yadda yadda) and now we have a bleed of 3 on stealth. Not everyone that bounces is cap 6 or less and every bleed this deck makes is a hefty one.
>
Well, stealth or block fails, yes you need that. But the thing is, bleeding for 3 is fairly responsible. And how many flicks is he going to have? Surely you get to cancel one or so and surely your grandprey will have some way to deal with pool damage of his own.

I mean, sure if you run into a guy with 10/70 deflections and a grandprey that plays, like, no flick and no poolgain then that kinda sucks, but in general that doesn't really happen since people play decks that can oust other people without relying on a IC bleeder in their back.

That said, I did change the deck when I played it. I put an emphasis on Corazon and Fanchon (by removing Adana since she's the worst draw you can get and if you can field 3 IC's you have already won anyway). Both sport AUS CEL DOM OBF, which I used to slot in Crocodile's Tongue (in favor of Majesties). I also played more Elder Impersonations because block fails is really good and I changed the Wash and a Villein for an Anarch Troublemaker too.

Worked like a charm.
